hero.headline: One prompt library
hero.intro: Stop passing good prompts around in chat threads. AI Hub gives your team one searchable place for prompts, custom agents and skills. Take the code free and set it up yourself, or have me set it up and fill it for you.

rows.before: The best prompts live in one person's notes or a chat thread nobody can search.
rows.after: Every prompt sits in one directory your team can search and filter by category and AI tool.

rows.before: Each person rewrites the same prompt, and gets different results.
rows.after: Templates have blanks to fill in, so everyone starts from the same wording and adds their own details.

rows.before: Nobody knows which version is the current one.
rows.after: Each prompt has one page, kept as a file in your own repository, so there is one place to edit and one version to copy.

service.label: The done-for-you service
service.headline: What I do, and what I don't.
paragraphs: I deploy your library, set it up with your branding on your domain, write the prompts, agents and skills your team needs, and train your people to use it. You get the code, so it is yours.

I don't offer ongoing maintenance. Once the project is handed over, your team or your own developer looks after it. Because every team's needs are different, the price comes from a custom quote after we talk.

items.question: How much does it cost?
items.answer: The code is free. If you want me to set it up, I quote per project, because the work depends on your branding, how many prompts you need and how much training you want. Send a request and I will reply with a quote.

items.question: Where is it hosted?
items.answer: Anywhere that serves static files. That includes GitHub Pages, Netlify, Vercel and your own server. If you hire me, I deploy it to the host you choose, on your domain.

items.question: What happens to our data?
items.answer: The site is static, so there is no database and no user accounts. Your prompts are files in your own repository. The only thing that leaves the site is the contact or submission form, which sends through Web3Forms, and you can remove those forms if you don't want them.

items.question: Do we need a developer?
items.answer: For the free version, it helps to have one, or someone comfortable with the command line. With the done-for-you service you don't need one to get started. Adding a prompt afterwards means creating a text file, and the README explains how.

items.question: Can we use it commercially?
items.answer: Yes. The project uses the MIT license, which allows business use if you keep the license notice. The theme code in src/components/kojima adds a Commons Clause: you can use it in your own site, but you can't resell the template as is.

items.question: How long does setup take?
items.answer: It depends on scope. A branded site with a few prompts is a smaller job than one with many custom agents and training for several teams. I will give you a timeline when I send the quote.

items.question: Can we take it over ourselves later?
items.answer: Yes, and that is the plan. You get the code in your own repository, and it is the same free, open source project. Your team can keep adding entries or change the site without me.

items.question: Is there support?
items.answer: I don't offer ongoing maintenance or support contracts. During your project I am available to you. For the free version, you can report bugs or ask for features on GitHub, and I will look when I can.
